title: Concurrency & scale via Locust
description:
Distinct from EPIC-14, which measures a single operation in isolation — this epic measures what happens when many of them run at once. Builds the Locust harness with the documented gevent-threadpool workaround for `ibm_db`'s blocking C extension (BM-12), then the single most important story in the whole benchmarking effort per BENCHMARK_STRATEGY.md's own framing: porting the cross-scope-leakage assertions out of the existing `benchmarks/isolation_load/run.py` into a Locust `User` scaled to 100 tenants x 1,000 agents x 200 users (BM-13) — this SDK's core differentiator and, per the strategy doc, its most important gate. Also covers the broader scalability sweeps (user ramp, agent-count ramp, mixed read/write, long-session sweep — BM-14) and connection-pool saturation characterization, the SDK's primary scalability ceiling per the capability inventory's E1 row (BM-15).

**Sequencing note on BM-13.** Its own deliverable list says to delete `benchmarks/isolation_load/` once the port is done. EPIC-12's BRUN-4 is the first-ever execution of that exact module (`--suite isolation --tenants 20 --workers 40`) and is still "To Do". If BRUN-4 has not run by the time BM-13 starts, either run BRUN-4 first against the existing module, or re-scope BRUN-4 to execute BM-13's new Locust-based isolation test instead and record that substitution explicitly in BENCHMARKS.md — do not let the module disappear with no isolation run ever recorded. Depends on EPIC-13 (BM-4).
